subject: math

entries: The probability scale: the marker slides from 0 (impossible) through 1/2 (an even chance) to 1 (certain), and every probability sits somewhere on this line.
slots.label: The probability scale
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: One value, three forms: the fair coin's 1/2 is the same value as 0.5 and 50% - one probability, three ways to write it.
slots.label: One value, three forms
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: P(event) = favourable over total: with five outcomes and three favourable, the gold dots gather 3 into the favourable chip and 5 into the total chip, building 3/5.
slots.label: P(event) = favourable over total
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Two tosses, one table: the grid draws itself and four dots travel in - heads-heads, heads-tails, tails-heads, tails-tails - one outcome per cell.
slots.label: Two tosses, one table
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Fill the table, multiply the branches: each cell is equally likely at 1/4, and heads-then-heads is 1/2 times 1/2, which is 1/4.
slots.label: Fill the table, multiply the branches
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: The gambler's slip: coins have no memory: three heads land in a row, yet the next toss is still an even chance, 1/2 each.
slots.label: The gambler's slip
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: A number between 0 and 1 that measures how likely an event is: 0 means impossible and 1 means certain.
slots.label: Probability
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: One possible result of a trial, such as heads on a single coin toss.
slots.label: Outcome
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A set of outcomes we are interested in, such as throwing exactly one head in two tosses.
slots.label: Event
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: Outcomes that share the same probability, like the four cells of the two-toss table at 1/4 each.
slots.label: Equally likely
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The set of all possible outcomes of a trial - for two coin tosses it has four members.
slots.label: Sample space
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: Events where the result of one does not change the probabilities of the other, so their probabilities multiply.
slots.label: Independent events
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

title: E-Math probability: single and combined events
